bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Uses PPP/DBFOT and government land-award structures (e.g., the Meghalaya 30-year DBFOT project, the Lakshadweep 5(+2)-year tent work order) to add rooms/tents without acquiring the underlying land, framed by the company as 'Fixed-Rent Asset Optimization.'
- Consolidated net worth grew from ₹287.84 Cr (FY24) to ₹449.15 Cr (FY26) and fixed assets from ₹205.55 Cr to ₹540.33 Cr, consistent with a capex-led expansion phase; FY26 consolidated debt-to-equity was still low at 0.13x.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Experiential tourism and hospitality company built around eco-responsible luxury stays, destination-led experiences and tourism infrastructure, using a lightweight, design-led accommodation model that avoids permanent construction and helps preserve local ecosystems.
- Describes itself as India's first-mover in luxury, non-permanent glamping resorts across ecologically sensitive regions (Rann of Kutch, Varanasi, Diu, Meghalaya).
- Third-party brand alliances lend distribution and credibility: IHCL manages 'Praveg Atoll', Bangaram under its Taj SeleQtions brand and partners with Ginger (an IHCL brand) at Jalandhar Circuit House, Diu; Mahindra Holidays & Resorts (MHRIL) has been allocated 13 fixed + 38 floating rooms across Daman, Ayodhya and Thinnakara.
- Also frames itself as a 'Mega-Exhibitions to Luxury Hospitality' player, drawing on two decades of experience executing government/corporate events, exhibitions and celebration venues within short timelines.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Praveg holds a 51% stake in Abhik Advertising (established 2008) and Bidhan Advertising (50+ year legacy, acquired 2016-17), adding INS/IBF-accredited advertising subsidiaries alongside the core hospitality/events business.
- [Government Tailwind] Deck cites government tourism-policy support: ₹2,541.06 Cr allocated to tourism infrastructure/skill development, 40 projects across 23 states to receive interest-free loans of ₹3,295.8 Cr, development of 50 top tourist destinations, and the Gyan Bharatam Mission to digitize over 1 Cr manuscripts.
- [Industry Backdrop] Deck cites third-party estimates for India's hospitality market (4.73% CAGR, Mordor Intelligence: USD 23.50 Bn in 2023 to USD 29.61 Bn by 2028) and the events/exhibition market (8.05% CAGR: USD 6.15 Bn in 2026 to USD 9.04 Bn by 2031), alongside India's Travel & Tourism Competitiveness Index rank improving from 65th (2013) to 39th (2024).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Praveg, established in 2005 as an event management company, has evolved into a hospitality brand offering luxury family resorts and boutique properties near sacred ghats, beaches, deserts and other scenic destinations, blending world-class comfort with cultural storytelling from pop-up luxury tents to 5-star vegetarian hotels. Beyond hospitality, the Company runs an Event & Exhibition Management business built since 2005, and an Advertising segment (Out-of-Home hoardings and smart-toilet advertising infrastructure) led by subsidiaries Abhik Advertising Pvt. Ltd. and Bidhan Advertising & Marketing Ltd.

outlook.body: Revenue growth: H2 to exceed H1 by >100% (historical seasonality + new revenue streams); Margin: EBITDA margin to improve to 25-30% in H2 due to operating leverage; Order inflow: INR50-70cr expected from events/advertising; Capex/commissioning: Thinnakara South (Dec 2025), Kutch expansion (Q1FY27), minimal new capex due to investor model
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR10cr+ from government and corporate events; 20+ weddings booked at Adalaj Theme Park; 252-bed Kutch asset awarded (equivalent to 126 rooms); ongoing bids for 5+ major exhibitions
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion via investor model (landowner + Praveg op) in Udaipur, Kihim, Kashi; potential museum/heritage tourism projects; government PPP bids for 5+ new destinations; digital advertising monopoly expansion in metro cities; international expansion into Africa
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen geographic presence and expand into untapped geographies across India and key global markets, growing the diversified hospitality/advertising/events portfolio.
- Bring sharper strategic focus to the Events & Exhibitions business — pursuing larger and more diverse opportunities — after temporary moderation while hospitality expanded.
- Expand the Out-of-Home advertising business into smart-toilet advertising infrastructure under PPP arrangements with municipal authorities.
- Scale the destination weddings and MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, Exhibitions) business with a more focused and aggressive approach.
- Pursue growth via targeted acquisitions, meaningful partnerships and steady organic expansion.
- Continue focus on innovation, operational excellence and digital transformation to strengthen competitive edge.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Praveg continued to expand and strengthen its portfolio of luxury resorts, tourism destinations, theme parks and hospitality projects across India. It commenced operations at Praveg Adalaj Theme Park (developed through wholly owned subsidiary Praveg Adalaj Tourism Infrastructure Private Limited under a PPP arrangement) in September 2025, intended to provide premium tourism, hospitality and event-related experiences. White Rann Resort was awarded an extension of 252 beds for 30 years. In February 2026, the Company received a Letter of Award from the Directorate of Tourism, Government of Meghalaya, for development, operation and maintenance of a minimum of 40 luxury cottages on approximately 10 acres at Umiam, Meghalaya, under DBFOT PPP mode with a 30-year concession period, intended to strengthen the Company's presence in the North-Eastern region. On the advertising side, the Company strengthened OOH advertising capacity by adding 310 hoardings covering 1,33,385 sq. ft. across India, and is expanding into smart-toilet advertising infrastructure under PPP arrangements, having secured exclusivity with the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation. The Company's growth-story timeline also lists an upcoming Safari Park at Serengeti, Tanzania.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian hospitality and tourism industry sustained growth momentum in FY26 on resilient domestic demand and gradual increase in inbound travel, with domestic travel the primary growth driver.
- Nationwide hotel occupancy estimated around 65%-70%, with RevPAR growth of 8%-12% year-on-year per industry reports, and upscale/luxury segments seeing strong demand from corporate travel, destination weddings, MICE events and inbound tourism.
- Tier II and Tier III cities and emerging leisure/wellness destinations continue to widen the industry's footprint, driving demand for quality accommodation and experiential offerings beyond metro hubs.
- Evolving consumer preference toward sustainability, wellness and immersive travel experiences continues to shape the sector, benefiting eco-friendly resorts, adventure tourism, wellness retreats and heritage stays.
- Government-led initiatives (e.g. Dekho Apna Desh, tourism infrastructure assistance, regional tourism circuits, last-mile connectivity investment) support inter-state and intra-state travel demand.
- Company's recent collaborations and investments in new properties and service offerings are expected to drive revenue growth and enhance brand presence across India and key global markets.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Praveg has rapidly expanded its resort footprint to 825+ rooms and relaunched its high-margin event/advertising business, but H1FY26 losses were driven by fixed PPP lease costs, new property ramp-up, and seasonal closures; profitability is expected to rebound sharply in H2 due to festive season demand and full-year contribution from newly commissioned assets.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: H2 to exceed H1 by >100% (historical seasonality + new revenue streams); Margin: EBITDA margin to improve to 25-30% in H2 due to operating leverage; Order inflow: INR50-70cr expected from events/advertising; Capex/commissioning: Thinnakara South (Dec 2025), Kutch expansion (Q1FY27), minimal new capex due to investor model

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian hospitality and tourism industry sustained growth momentum in FY26 on resilient domestic demand and gradual increase in inbound travel, with domestic travel the primary growth driver.
- Nationwide hotel occupancy estimated around 65%-70%, with RevPAR growth of 8%-12% year-on-year per industry reports, and upscale/luxury segments seeing strong demand from corporate travel, destination weddings, MICE events and inbound tourism.
- Tier II and Tier III cities and emerging leisure/wellness destinations continue to widen the industry's footprint, driving demand for quality accommodation and experiential offerings beyond metro hubs.
- Evolving consumer preference toward sustainability, wellness and immersive travel experiences continues to shape the sector, benefiting eco-friendly resorts, adventure tourism, wellness retreats and heritage stays.
- Government-led initiatives (e.g. Dekho Apna Desh, tourism infrastructure assistance, regional tourism circuits, last-mile connectivity investment) support inter-state and intra-state travel demand.
- Company's recent collaborations and investments in new properties and service offerings are expected to drive revenue growth and enhance brand presence across India and key global markets.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Fixed PPP lease costs (non-negotiable, same across seasons); high fixed labor cost (1,500+ in-house staff vs. outsourced); depreciation INR15.98cr in H1; incremental H2 margin contribution ~75% due to low variable costs; seasonal resorts closed in Q2 added cost without revenue

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing investor-funded expansion (70%+ future growth); minimal debt reliance (only INR10-15cr bank limits); retained earnings used for operational ramp-up; warrant forfeiture (INR500cr+) converted to reserves; no dividend policy announced

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Praveg continued to expand and strengthen its portfolio of luxury resorts, tourism destinations, theme parks and hospitality projects across India. It commenced operations at Praveg Adalaj Theme Park (developed through wholly owned subsidiary Praveg Adalaj Tourism Infrastructure Private Limited under a PPP arrangement) in September 2025, intended to provide premium tourism, hospitality and event-related experiences. White Rann Resort was awarded an extension of 252 beds for 30 years. In February 2026, the Company received a Letter of Award from the Directorate of Tourism, Government of Meghalaya, for development, operation and maintenance of a minimum of 40 luxury cottages on approximately 10 acres at Umiam, Meghalaya, under DBFOT PPP mode with a 30-year concession period, intended to strengthen the Company's presence in the North-Eastern region. On the advertising side, the Company strengthened OOH advertising capacity by adding 310 hoardings covering 1,33,385 sq. ft. across India, and is expanding into smart-toilet advertising infrastructure under PPP arrangements, having secured exclusivity with the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation. The Company's growth-story timeline also lists an upcoming Safari Park at Serengeti, Tanzania.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, long-term oriented, defensive on financial guidance; emphasizes operational milestones over short-term P&L; dismisses stock price volatility as 'emotional'; highlights corporate governance and compliance; optimistic on H2 recovery and investor model scalability

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- distribution: Wide network of travel agents across online and offline channels across India — evidence: company describes itself as having 'A Wide Network Of Travel Agents Online & Oﬄine - Across India' as a core competence
- integration: In-house creative studio and department of architects supporting project design and execution — evidence: listed under 'Our Core Competence' as an in-house capability
- customer lock-in: Long-term association with tourism stakeholders built over 20+ years — evidence: '20+ Years Of Experience' and 'Long-term Association With Tourism' cited as core competence

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Seasonal revenue volatility (Q2 losses); PPP lease inflexibility; delayed CRZ clearances for Kihim/Kashi; reliance on government event tenders; high fixed labor cost structure; brand perception risk from vegetarian-only policy in luxury segment

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Adalaj Theme Park’s 1M+ social media reach and wedding bookings represent a low-cost, high-margin experiential revenue stream beyond traditional rooms; Kutch expansion uses stranded Varanasi assets — effectively zero capex for 126 rooms; advertising revenue from Abhik & Bidhan is now larger than event management revenue and growing faster

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen geographic presence and expand into untapped geographies across India and key global markets, growing the diversified hospitality/advertising/events portfolio.
- Bring sharper strategic focus to the Events & Exhibitions business — pursuing larger and more diverse opportunities — after temporary moderation while hospitality expanded.
- Expand the Out-of-Home advertising business into smart-toilet advertising infrastructure under PPP arrangements with municipal authorities.
- Scale the destination weddings and MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, Exhibitions) business with a more focused …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Praveg holds a 51% stake in Abhik Advertising (established 2008) and Bidhan Advertising (50+ year legacy, acquired 2016-17), adding INS/IBF-accredited advertising subsidiaries alongside the core hospitality/events business.
- [Government Tailwind] Deck cites government tourism-policy support: ₹2,541.06 Cr allocated to tourism infrastructure/skill development, 40 projects across 23 states to receive interest-free loans of ₹3,295.8 Cr, development of 50 top tourist destinations, and the Gyan Bharatam Mission to digitize over 1 Cr manuscripts.
- [Industry Backdrop] Deck cites third-party estimates for India's hospitality market (4.73% CAGR, Mordor Intelligence: USD 23.50 Bn in 2023 to USD 29.61 Bn by 2028) and the events/exhibition market (8.05% CAGR: USD 6.15 Bn in 2026 to USD 9.04 Bn by 2031), alongside India's Travel & Tourism Competitiveness Index rank improving from 65th (2013) to 39th (2024).

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

hero.oneLiner: Praveg is an experiential hospitality company operating 17 luxury resorts and boutique properties across India under an Asset Light Model, alongside Event & Exhibition management and an Out-of-Home advertising business.
